soc-1.theory: Cybersecurity protects the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems and data. A Security Operations Center (SOC) is the team and process for monitoring security events, investigating alerts, and coordinating response. Analysts compare observations across sources, preserve evidence, and escalate findings under agreed procedures. Start here by learning how an operating system records account activity.
soc-1.example: A successful service logon differs from an interactive sign-in even when both share event 4624.
soc-1.relevance: Authentication auditing makes account activity visible and helps analysts separate evidence from assumptions.
soc-1.analysis: Distinguish interactive sign-in from privilege assignment and sign-out using Event IDs.
soc-1.motivation: Your SOC journey has begun. Reading your first audit records is a practical step toward understanding how security teams protect systems.
